answer: An orchard defence groups identities the way a grower groups trees sharing one root system: accounts linked by funding, timing, or near-identical behaviour are clustered and their combined voting and earning weight is capped, however many names they use. At its nadir, a whisper campaign of thousands of look-alike agents therefore counts no more than one honest agent. To break out, an attacker must fund each copy separately, stagger its actions, and grow a distinct history — paying the full cost, in money and time, for every extra identity.
